# SpotVault

> Free app that keeps your music offline. The Windows app saves playlists from Spotify, YouTube, YouTube Music and SoundCloud as audio files with cover art, one folder per playlist, and can search for any single song and save it into a playlist. The Android and iPhone app copies those playlists from the PC over Wi-Fi, plays them with no signal, and can add new songs by search (the PC downloads them and sends them back).

- Website: https://sarath-apps.vercel.app/spotvault/
- Source code: https://github.com/sarathlal-12/spotvault
- Downloads (v2.0.1): https://github.com/sarathlal-12/spotvault/releases/tag/v2.0.1
- Price: free. No account needed; everything runs locally.
- Platforms: Windows (installer), Android (APK), iPhone (IPA, sideloaded with AltStore)
- Author: Sarath Lal (https://github.com/sarathlal-12)

## How it works

1. Paste a public playlist link (Spotify, YouTube, YouTube Music or SoundCloud) into SpotVault on Windows. It saves every song with cover art into its own folder. Later syncs only fetch new songs.
2. Use Search songs to find any single track, and save it into one of your playlists.
3. Click Connect phone on the PC. The phone app connects over the same Wi-Fi using the PC's address and a 6-digit PIN, and copies every playlist across. Interrupted copies resume.
4. On the phone, Search > Find new songs lets you listen to a song and save it to a playlist; the PC downloads it and sends it back over Wi-Fi.
5. Play offline on the phone: playlists, Liked Songs, search, shuffle, repeat, queue editing, sleep timer, playback speed and lock-screen controls.

## Notes

- Playlists must be public or shared by link; private playlists can't be read.
- Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi, and Windows Firewall must allow SpotVault on Private networks.
- The Windows app has everything built in (including the audio converter); nothing else to install.
- Not on the Google Play Store or Apple App Store; it is distributed through GitHub releases.

# AirBridge

> Free Windows app that plays your phone's audio through the PC's speakers or headphones. iPhone sends audio over AirPlay (Wi-Fi); Android (and iPhone) over Bluetooth, with the PC acting as a Bluetooth speaker. Runs in the system tray; the iPhone's volume buttons control it.

- Website: https://sarath-apps.vercel.app/airbridge/
- Source code: https://github.com/sarathlal-12/airbridge
- Downloads (v1.0.1): https://github.com/sarathlal-12/airbridge/releases/tag/v1.0.1
- Price: free. No account; audio stays on the home network.
- Platforms: Windows 10 (2004) and 11, 64-bit. Nothing to install on the phone.

# .light

> Free Windows app: a small black island at the top of the screen, in the spirit of the iPhone's Dynamic Island. Hover it or press Alt+Space. Music controls with live sound waves, clipboard history, Claude Code status (shows when a session needs permission, is working or has finished, with a Claude tab listing every session), phone notifications from Android or iPhone through Phone Link (with Copy buttons for login codes, calls and phone battery), phone-to-PC copy and paste (Android through Phone Link, iPhone through a one-tap Apple Shortcut), a screenshot moment you can drag into any app, camera and mic in-use dots, charging, download and update moments, prompt snippets that paste into the last app, Grab text (Ctrl+Alt+T, Windows' own offline text recognition) and Grab image (Ctrl+Alt+S), a file shelf, focus timer, notes and a File lab for converting images and making PDFs. Optional fun switches: an island pet, shy mode, typing fire, confetti, a rage-click detector, a CPU/GPU mood ring with temperatures, touch grass, night owl and a drink-water reminder. Each feature can be switched off.

- Website: https://sarath-apps.vercel.app/light/
- Source code: https://github.com/sarathlal-12/light
- Downloads (v1.4.0): https://github.com/sarathlal-12/light/releases/tag/v1.4.0
- Price: free, MIT license. No account; everything stays on the PC.
- Platforms: Windows 10 (2004) and 11, 64-bit.

# Byterake

> Free, offline disk cleaner for Windows. Shows total, used and free space, measures a built-in cleanup catalog (temp files, the Recycle Bin, Chrome/Edge/Firefox cache folders, thumbnail cache, crash dumps, Windows Update and Delivery Optimization caches, npm/pip/NuGet caches), lists old installers and large files to tick one by one, scans drives into a sorted folder tree, and opens programs' own uninstallers. Nothing is removed until the user confirms the exact count and size; files go to the Recycle Bin by default. A built-in never-touch list protects System32, WinSxS, Program Files, pagefile/hiberfil/swapfile, Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Videos, Music, .git folders, system files, and links and junctions. No network, no AI, no telemetry.

- Website: https://sarath-apps.vercel.app/byterake/
- Source code: https://github.com/sarathlal-12/byterake
- Downloads (v1.0.0): https://github.com/sarathlal-12/byterake/releases/tag/v1.0.0
- Price: free, MIT license. No account; nothing leaves the PC.
- Platforms: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit (installer).
